research_text:
# Research brief

## API and finding

`javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec` holds a password and, depending on the constructor, parameters used to derive a password-based encryption key. For its four-argument constructor, the third argument is `iterationCount`; the fourth is the requested derived-key length. The three-argument constructor also has an iteration count as its third argument. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html))

The supplied CrySL file’s four-argument construction event binds that third argument to `iterationCount` and sets the constraint `iterationCount >= 10000`. That is a **rule threshold**, not a documented Java API minimum: Oracle documents rejection of a nonpositive iteration count, not all counts below 10,000. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

## Documented usage and remediation

- Oracle documents that the parameterized constructors reject a null or empty salt and a nonpositive iteration count; the four-argument constructor also rejects a nonpositive key length. It documents the three-argument constructor for fixed-key-size PBE ciphers and the four-argument constructor for variable-key-size PBE ciphers. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html))
- Oracle recommends using a character array rather than a `String` for a password so its contents can be overwritten. `clearPassword()` clears the specification’s internal password copy; callers are responsible for clearing copies returned by `getPassword()`. The constructor itself clones the password and salt. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))
- The CrySL file additionally requires `randomized[salt]`, constrains the password with `neverTypeOf` and `notHardCoded`, and orders construction before `clearPassword()`. These are rule requirements, distinct from the Javadoc’s constructor-validity checks. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

The Javadoc does **not** prescribe 10,000 or a specific remediation for an otherwise valid positive count below it. To satisfy the stated CrySL constraint, the bound `iterationCount` must meet the rule’s minimum; that alone is not an Oracle assertion that 10,000 is appropriate for every use. RFC 8018 separately recommends selecting a work factor appropriate to the environment and acceptable user latency. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html))

## Compatibility and migration

Oracle’s JCA guide says PBE decryption must use the same parameters as encryption and documents retrieving and storing encoded algorithm parameters. `SealedObject` is documented as attaching the sealing parameters to the encrypted contents. Thus, changing a count used to create data is a compatibility concern for readers of that data; the documentation does not establish the format or behavior of any particular application. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/crypto/CryptoSpec.html?source=:so:ch:or:awr::::PrivateEndpointsPlaybook))

RFC 8018 specifies formats in which PBKDF2 parameters include the salt and iteration count. Those formats are **not automatically established** merely by using `PBEKeySpec`; a persisted or wire format depends on the surrounding scheme. ([rfc-editor.org](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8018/?utm_source=openai))

Oracle documents `PBEKeySpec` as available since Java 1.4. That does not by itself establish availability of a particular algorithm, provider, format, or count on every platform. The cited `PBEKeySpec` documentation does not provide a migration procedure for previously persisted data or a wire protocol. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html))

## Exact rule source and matching limits

The supplied file declares `SPEC javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec`. Its event and constraint clauses are, verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

```text
	c1: PBEKeySpec(password, salt, iterationCount, keyLength);
	Con := c1;

	cp1: clearPassword();
	ClearPass := cp1;
```

```text
	iterationCount >= 10000;
```

The file declares the four event variables as `char[]`, `byte[]`, `int`, and `int`, respectively. It therefore **states a four-parameter construction event** and a zero-parameter `clearPassword` event; it also lists the one- and three-argument constructors under `FORBIDDEN`. It does not state a general, unconstrained name-only matching clause. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

**Can it match a method that merely shares a name?** The file alone does not specify the analyzer’s receiver-type resolution or matching implementation, so that behavior cannot be determined from this source alone. In particular, the `SPEC` declaration identifies the governed type, but the file does not independently document how an analyzer excludes or includes unrelated same-name methods.

The URL refers to the moving `master` branch. The supplied SHA-256 was not independently verified in this research pass, and the file does not identify the detector version or its data-flow semantics.

## Direct sources

- CrySL rule: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl
- Oracle `PBEKeySpec` API: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html
- Oracle JCA reference guide: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/18/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html
- RFC 8018, PKCS #5: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8018.html
